ArcRaidersHub: Where to Find Amplification Modules

intro.summary: Amplification takes a fully upgraded tier IV weapon one step further, to level V. You spend a matching Amplification Module to activate it, then research and buy upgrades that change how the weapon behaves. This guide explains the system, where Raiders report finding each material, and how sure we are about every number.

what.text: Amplification is the level V weapon upgrade added in Frozen Trail 2.0. It raises maximum durability from 130 to 200 and opens a short tree of weapon-specific upgrades such as new fire modes, ammo types, magazines and optics.
Fifteen weapons can be amplified at launch; Stiletto and Bantam cannot. Each weapon needs the module that matches its original rarity, from Mk. I for common weapons to Mk. V for legendary ones.
Amplified weapons are only repaired with Amplified Fragments, and they drop to around 10% durability when you go down, so plan for repairs before you farm.

steps.activate: Bring the weapon to tier IV, then spend one matching Amplification Module at the Gunsmith (level IV) to amplify it.
steps.upgrade: Each upgrade has a research project (5,000 research points, a task and ARC parts) and an install cost in amplification materials.
steps.repair: Repair amplified weapons with Amplified Fragments from recycling amplified gear.

branches.text: Some upgrades require another one first; for example, Rattler Drum Mag requires More Reload, and Aphelion Increased Burst requires Charged Burst.
Some upgrades exclude each other. For example, Bettina Bigger Mag and Semi-Auto cannot both be active, and Hairpin Incendiary Rounds closes the Semi-Auto and Tracker Rounds branches.
Upgrade choices are permanent; they cannot be reverted. The Amplification Hunt only lets you pick combinations that can exist together.

prerequisites.text: Unlock the Outpost and expand it to level 4.
Upgrade the Gunsmith to level IV (3 Radial Press, 3 Magnetic Accelerator, 1 Emperor Modulator).
Upgrade the Research Station to level 4 to open Amplified Research.
Bring the weapon to tier IV first.
Have the Amplification Module that matches the weapon’s rarity.

openQuestions.text: Burletta and Canto Sprint Shooting: 4 Fluted Rotor Core (wiki) vs 3 (Raider Network cheat sheet). The Hunt totals use 4.
Do spare Amplification Modules recycle into 7 Amplified Fragments? Four sources say yes; the wiki says modules cannot be recycled.
Eight upgrades (e.g. Bigger Mag, More Reload, Full-Auto) list no research project in game-file sources, but an older wiki page names one for each.
Mobile-Fire Grip Fittings research (Sprint Shooting): Skulker Drivers vs Skulker Targeters, and the quantity, differ between sources.
Some community guides list extra exclusions for Rattler, Renegade and Burletta that the wiki does not.
ARC Frigate maps: one source includes Riven Tides, a game-file list excludes it.
Propellant Valve Assembly and Fluted Rotor Core locations rest on tracker data and one report each.
Which maps can roll the Electromagnetic Storm, and where the Matriarch drops its reactor, are not verified.
Effect descriptions come from the community wiki and guides, not from the game client.
No source publishes drop rates. We do not show any.

locations.name: ARC Frigate
locations.what: A huge airborne ARC vessel added in Frozen Trail 2.0. It is a PvPvE encounter guarded by Hydra turrets, and its hull and cargo are the main confirmed source of Amplification Modules.

Where.text: Appears as a rotating map condition. Sources disagree on Riven Tides: one lists it, a game-file list excludes it. Neither lists Stella Montis.

Access.text: No key needed. Board by riding one of the smaller Reclaimers up to the ship. The squad pulls three levers to raise the core, shoots the exposed Power Cores, then opens Cargo.

Loot.text: Breach & Search ports on the hull and interior, plus the dropped cargo canister. Ports are picked clean quickly by other squads.

Tips.text: Bring a squad and a grappling tool. The condition removes locked doors and Raider Hatches and lowers ground loot value. No drop rates are published.

locations.name: Fallen Emperor
locations.what: The downed ARC Emperor is the biggest landmark on Pendola Pass. Its interior is a key-gated run of randomized trial rooms ending in a hangar, and it is the second confirmed source of Amplification Modules.

Access.text: Insert an Emperor Gateway Conduit (single-use key) into the socket at the base hatch. The conduit is crafted from its blueprint plus three ARC couplers that come from Redirection payloads.

Inside.text: Around a dozen randomized trial rooms with breachable wall panels and carrier hatches; the final hangar has more containers. Opening the hatch is loud and a timer warning plays at 10 minutes left.

Also drops.text: Emperor Modulator, needed for the Gunsmith IV upgrade that unlocks amplification.

locations.name: Emperor Payloads & Redirection
locations.what: During the Redirection condition on Pendola Pass, Raiders search Damaged Emperor Relays for an Emperor Beacon and use it to call down a payload. The payload’s main container is the confirmed source of Pneumatic Actuators and Pressure Regulators.

How it works.text: Find an active Damaged Emperor Relay (shown on the map), take the Emperor Beacon from it, then call in the payload and defend it while it opens.

Name.text: Most guides call it an Emperor Payload; two call it a Harvester Payload, and the wiki item page says Harvester Payload.

Also drops.text: Emperor Gateway Conduit blueprint and the ARC couplers used to craft the Fallen Emperor key (not guaranteed).

Watch out.text: Sources disagree on whether the couplers can be stored between raids. An Emperor Beacon is worthless after extraction.

locations.name: Pendola Pass
locations.what: The frozen mountain map added in Frozen Trail 2.0. It hosts the Fallen Emperor and the Redirection payloads, and one report places a Fluted Rotor Core in an exterior hatch.

Name.text: The in-game name is Pendola Pass.

Exterior find.text: One guide found a Fluted Rotor Core in a sealed round wall hatch (Breach & Search) on a high exterior ledge above the snowy valley.

Doors.text: Some doors are frozen shut and open with a fire source.

Storms.text: Whether the Electromagnetic Storm can occur here is not verified.

locations.name: Electromagnetic Storm
locations.what: A weather condition with lightning strikes. Fossilized Lightning can appear at the strike point; it is not a container drop.

How.text: Watch for blue sparks a few seconds before a strike, then search the impact crater for a jagged stone.

Chance.text: Community reports describe the chance per strike as low; no number is published.

Maps.text: Which maps can roll the storm is not verified.

locations.name: ARC Assessor
locations.what: A large three-legged ARC landing platform that appears during the Close Scrutiny condition. Its containers are the only confirmed source of Assessor Matrix.

Maps.text: Dam Battlegrounds, Spaceport, Buried City and The Blue Gate.

Loot.text: Three breachable containers; only one can be breached at a time. Breaching sounds an alarm that brings Vaporizers and Rocketeers, and the Assessor flies off if you wait too long.

locations.name: The Queen
locations.what: Boss-class ARC that appears during Harvester events and drops the Queen Reactor.

Loot.text: Queen Reactors come from the wreck and leg loot. Frozen Trail moved higher-tier loot from the leg armor plates into the legs themselves.

Maps.text: Our catalog lists Dam Battlegrounds, Spaceport and The Blue Gate from community drop tables.

locations.name: Matriarch
locations.what: Boss-class ARC that drops the Matriarch Reactor. Destroy the frontal faceplates to expose the core, then loot the wreck quickly.

Loot.text: Exactly which part drops the reactor is not stated by our sources.

Maps.text: Our catalog lists Dam Battlegrounds, Spaceport and The Blue Gate from community drop tables.

locations.name: ARC Turbine
locations.what: A flying ARC that lands mid-raid on three legs, exposing yellow canisters as weak points. Its remains are the reported source of Turbine Compressor.

Loot.text: Scavenge the destroyed Turbine. One tracker also lists ARC Courier and Harvester containers.

locations.name: Recycling amplified gear
locations.what: Amplified Fragments do not drop from containers. They come from recycling or salvaging amplified gear.

Sources.text: Recycling or salvaging an amplified weapon (a fully built Aphelion reportedly recycles to 35), or recycling an old Anvil Splitter mod (retired in 2.0).

Spare modules.text: Four sources say a spare Amplification Module recycles into 7 Amplified Fragments; the wiki module pages say modules cannot be recycled.
